argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification position than an unconditional clean release. Aggregate readiness passed and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports release readiness overall, but the logistics customs triage weakness remains exposed and is not cured by rollout controls alone. The supportable position is certification conditioned on explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of that limitation, with monitoring and rollback treated as operational mitigations rather than substitutes for disclosure. On that reading, the packet is not trying to evade the policy threshold; it is aligning the certification decision to the policy by making the disclosure obligation explicit.
claims_about_business_cost: No urgency claim is needed. The relevant point is narrower: when the remaining issue is a specific disclosure precondition rather than evidence of severe launch failure, it is disproportionate to treat the entire certification packet as if it depended on rollout controls alone. A bounded caveat and compliance condition addresses the actual gap without unnecessary escalation.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is clear that rollout controls and post-launch monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed and there is no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. The same admissible evidence also shows what compliance requires here: because the weakness remains in scope for the named launch use case, certification is supportable only as a caveated decision tied to completing the required model-card disclosure before launch. The actor concedes that any unconditional claim of present full compliance would be overbroad.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show that the required model-card disclosure has already been completed.
The rollout starts at 6% with rollback capability, but those controls do not exclude the affected logistics customs triage segment.
The risk-acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the specific logistics customs triage exposure.
An unconditional statement that certification is already fully compliant on the present record would go beyond the evidence.
